extra.message: Affected versions of aiohttp are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. aiohttp WebSocket endpoints fail to enforce the max_msg_size memory limit when a peer sends large incomplete WebSocket frame payloads. An attacker (a malicious client against a server endpoint, or a malicious server against a client connection) can send oversized incomplete frames to bypass the size limit and exhaust memory, causing denial of service. Any use of aiohttp server-side WebSocketResponse endpoints or client-side ws_connect connections reaches the vulnerable frame parser.

extra.message: Affected versions of aiohttp are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. The optimized C HTTP parser in aiohttp validates each fragment of an HTTP request/response line individually against max_line_size instead of the accumulated total. An attacker can split an oversized line across multiple network reads, bypassing the limit and causing excessive memory consumption, leading to denial of service. This affects both server-side request-target parsing and client-side response reason-phrase parsing.

extra.message: Affected versions of starlette are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). Serving static files with Starlette's StaticFiles app on Windows resolves requested paths with os.path.realpath() before checking directory containment. extra.message: Affected versions of starlette are vulnerable to Improper Validation of Unsafe Equivalence in Input / Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling'). Starlette reconstructs `request.url` (and `request.base_url`) from the unvalidated HTTP `Host` header. An attacker can send a malformed `Host` header containing `/`, `?`, or `#` to shift the parsed path/query boundaries, making `request.url.path` diverge from the path the ASGI server actually routed against. Middleware or endpoints that apply path-based security restrictions using `request.url` can be bypassed.

cwe: CWE-1289: Improper Validation of Unsafe Equivalence in Input

extra.message: Affected versions of starlette are vulnerable to Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code ('Unsafe Reflection'). Starlette resolves HTTPEndpoint request handlers by lowercasing the client-supplied HTTP method and looking it up as an instance attribute with getattr(), without restricting the lookup to standard HTTP verbs. An attacker can send a non-standard HTTP method (e.g. `_DO_DELETE`) whose lowercased name matches an internal helper method (e.g. `_do_delete`) on an HTTPEndpoint subclass, invoking that method as if it were a request handler and bypassing the authorization checks applied by the intended public handlers.

cwe: CWE-470: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code ('Unsafe Reflection')

extra.message: Affected versions of tornado are vulnerable to Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor. Tornado's SimpleAsyncHTTPClient (the default client behind AsyncHTTPClient/HTTPClient) forwards the Authorization, Cookie, auth_username, and auth_password values, as well as credentials embedded in the request URL (user:password@host), to the redirect target when following a 3xx redirect to a different origin. An attacker who controls or can influence a redirect response can capture credentials intended for the original origin whenever an authenticated request follows redirects.

extra.message: Affected versions of tornado are vulnerable to Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor / Operation on a Resource after Expiration or Release. The optional CurlAsyncHTTPClient backend pools and reuses pycurl handles without fully resetting them between requests. Per-request client TLS certificates (SSLCERT/SSLKEY), proxy basic-auth credentials (PROXYUSERPWD), and network interface bindings (INTERFACE) can persist onto later requests on the same client that did not set them, leaking credentials to unintended hosts.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
CWE-672: Operation on a Resource after Expiration or Release
metadata.sca-reachable-if: you issue requests with differing per-request credentials or configuration through a shared CurlAsyncHTTPClient instance

extra.message: Affected versions of tornado are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification). Tornado does not enforce an overall limit on the cumulative size of gzip-decompressed data. A malicious server (when using the default `SimpleAsyncHTTPClient`/`AsyncHTTPClient`/`HTTPClient` to fetch responses) or a malicious client (when the `HTTPServer` is started with `decompress_request=True`) can supply a small, highly compressed payload that expands into effectively unlimited memory, causing a denial of service ("gzip bomb").

cwe: CWE-409: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)

extra.message: Affected versions of urllib3 are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification). urllib3 fails to enforce its decompression-bomb safeguards in two streaming-API code paths: (1) the second and subsequent HTTPResponse.read(amt=N) or HTTPResponse.stream(amt=N) calls on a Brotli-encoded response, and (2) HTTPResponse.drain_conn() invoked after the body has been partially decompressed. A malicious server can return a highly compressed payload to force the client to fully decompress it in a single operation, consuming excessive CPU and memory.

extra.message: Affected versions of urllib3 are vulnerable to Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.
